title: Relative latching maps give lifts of arbitrary ordinal diagrams
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a category admitting all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $\theta$ be any small ordinal, regarded as the category with one arrow $\beta\to\alpha$ precisely when $\beta\leq\alpha$. Let $D,E,U,V:\theta\to\mathcal B$ be functors and $f:D\to E$, $p:U\to V$ natural transformations. For $Z:\theta\to\mathcal B$ put $L_\alpha Z=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\alpha} Z_\beta$, with its canonical map to $Z_\alpha$. The induced maps define the relative latching map
$$\lambda_\alpha(f):D_\alpha\amalg_{L_\alpha D}L_\alpha E\longrightarrow E_\alpha,$$
where the pushout is the colimit of the displayed span. Suppose that, for every $\alpha<\theta$, $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ has the left lifting property against $p_\alpha$, with the diagonal property of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Then $f$ has the left lifting property against $p$ in the functor category: for every pair of natural transformations $s:D\to U$ and $t:E\to V$ satisfying $ps=tf$, there exists a natural transformation $h:E\to U$ with $hf=s$ and $ph=t$. No continuity condition is imposed on any of the four diagrams. The assertion includes the empty ordinal and requires no model structure or factorization system. All indexing categories are small in fixed universes, which may be enlarged.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison before the total inverse limit: cell induction on the unit for free dg diagrams; ordinal-stage lifting argument of lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison, original step 4; agent extraction of the transfinite lifting argument, not a Stacks homotopy-theoretic assertion.

external.place: Hovey, Model categories, Definition 5.1.1 and Proposition 5.1.4, printed pp. 120-121. The proof uses only pairwise ground lifting at each degree; the formulation here removes the unused model-category hypotheses. Read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix a square $ps=tf$. For $\beta\leq\alpha$ write $Z_{\beta\alpha}:Z_\beta\to Z_\alpha$ for the transition map of any of the four diagrams. A partial lift on $\{\beta:\beta<\alpha\}$ means maps $h_\beta:E_\beta\to U_\beta$ satisfying $h_\beta f_\beta=s_\beta$, $p_\beta h_\beta=t_\beta$, and $U_{\beta\gamma}h_\beta=h_\gamma E_{\beta\gamma}$ whenever $\beta\leq\gamma<\alpha$. At $\alpha=0$ this is the empty family. We show explicitly how to extend any such family by one component at $\alpha$, including when $\alpha$ is a nonzero limit ordinal.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, Definition 5.1.1, printed p. 120, and proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: compatible partial lifts on initial degree segments and the empty base. Agent specialization to the ordinal category with degree equal to the index.

proof.text:
Given this partial lift, the maps $a_\beta=U_{\beta\alpha}h_\beta:E_\beta\to U_\alpha$ form a cocone: for $\beta\leq\gamma<\alpha$,
$$a_\gamma E_{\beta\gamma}=U_{\gamma\alpha}h_\gamma E_{\beta\gamma}=U_{\gamma\alpha}U_{\beta\gamma}h_\beta=a_\beta.$$
The colimit universal property gives $a:L_\alpha E\to U_\alpha$. Let $d:L_\alpha D\to D_\alpha$ and $e:L_\alpha E\to E_\alpha$ be the structure maps and $\ell:L_\alpha D\to L_\alpha E$ the map induced by $f$. On each coprojection from $D_\beta$ we have
$$a\ell\iota^D_\beta=U_{\beta\alpha}h_\beta f_\beta=U_{\beta\alpha}s_\beta=s_\alpha D_{\beta\alpha}=s_\alpha d\iota^D_\beta.$$
Uniqueness in the colimit property gives $a\ell=s_\alpha d$. Applying the same property to the span defining $P_\alpha=D_\alpha\amalg_{L_\alpha D}L_\alpha E$ gives $q:P_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ with $qj_D=s_\alpha$ and $qj_E=a$. The span is finite and the predecessor category is small, so all these colimits exist.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, Definition 5.1.2, printed p. 120, and proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: the map from the latching object into the new right source and the relative-latching pushout. Cocone and pushout details supplied using Stacks Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit.

proof.text:
The map $q$ is the top of a square with left side $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ and bottom $t_\alpha$. Indeed, on the $D_\alpha$ leg,
$$p_\alpha qj_D=p_\alpha s_\alpha=t_\alpha f_\alpha=t_\alpha\lambda_\alpha(f)j_D.$$
On a coprojection from $E_\beta$ into the other leg, naturality of $p,t$ gives
$$p_\alpha a\iota^E_\beta=p_\alpha U_{\beta\alpha}h_\beta=V_{\beta\alpha}p_\beta h_\beta=V_{\beta\alpha}t_\beta=t_\alpha E_{\beta\alpha}=t_\alpha e\iota^E_\beta.$$
The universal property first of $L_\alpha E$ and then of the pushout therefore gives $p_\alpha q=t_\alpha\lambda_\alpha(f)$. These equality tests remain valid for an empty predecessor category: its colimit has a unique map to each object.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: commutativity of the relative-latching lifting square. Agent expansion of both leg identities using Stacks Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit.

proof.text:
Apply the assumed left lifting property of $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ against $p_\alpha$ to this square. Its diagonal is a map $h_\alpha:E_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ with $h_\alpha\lambda_\alpha(f)=q$ and $p_\alpha h_\alpha=t_\alpha$. Restriction to $j_D$ gives $h_\alpha f_\alpha=s_\alpha$. For every $\beta<\alpha$, restriction to $j_E\iota^E_\beta$ gives
$$h_\alpha E_{\beta\alpha}=h_\alpha\lambda_\alpha(f)j_E\iota^E_\beta=qj_E\iota^E_\beta=a\iota^E_\beta=U_{\beta\alpha}h_\beta.$$
Thus adjoining $h_\alpha$ extends the partial lift without changing any earlier component. In particular this is an extension at a limit object itself, rather than an assertion that $E_\alpha$ or $U_\alpha$ is the colimit of its predecessors.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: choose the new diagonal and extend the earlier partial lift. Agent generalization uses the assumed lifting property for this pair of maps directly.

proof.text: Use well-ordered recursion to make these extensions compatible for all $\alpha<\theta$. Here is a total recursion rule to which the cited statement applies. Take $\mathcal V$ to be the collection of all partial lifts on initial segments of $\theta$, including the empty one. Enlarge the universe if necessary; these families form a set since they are indexed by subsets of the small set $\theta$ and have components in the fixed hom sets. By choice fix one extension from step 4 for each valid input partial lift and next index. Given arbitrary $(v_\beta)_{\beta<\alpha}$ in $\mathcal V$, if each $v_\beta$ has domain $\{\gamma:\gamma\leq\beta\}$ and these families agree on overlaps, let $G_\alpha$ be the chosen extension at $\alpha$ of their union; otherwise let $G_\alpha$ be the empty partial lift. In the first case the union is a partial lift on $\{\gamma:\gamma<\alpha\}$: each equation involves at most two indices and is verified in a $v_\beta$ containing them. The cited recursion theorem gives $v_\alpha=G_\alpha((v_\beta)_{\beta<\alpha})$. Well-ordered induction verifies that $v_\alpha$ always has domain $\{\gamma:\gamma\leq\alpha\}$ and extends every $v_\beta$ with $\beta<\alpha$: the earlier families agree because the larger one extends the smaller one, so the first branch applies. At $0$ the union is empty, and at a limit index it is just the union of already chosen components. The only colimits in the construction are those of steps 2 and 3; no continuity of a diagram is needed.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: transfinite construction and agreement on initial segments. Agent implementation by the existing well-ordered-recursion node, with a total rule and an explicit invariant.

proof.text: For nonempty $\theta$, define $h_\alpha$ to be the $\alpha$-component of $v_\alpha$. Compatibility of the partial lifts implies that $v_\gamma$ has this same $\alpha$-component whenever $\alpha\leq\gamma$. Consequently, for every $\alpha\leq\gamma<\theta$, the partial-lift equations in $v_\gamma$ give $U_{\alpha\gamma}h_\alpha=h_\gamma E_{\alpha\gamma}$. Thus the components define a natural transformation $h:E\to U$, and its component equations give $hf=s$ and $ph=t$. If $\theta=0$, the unique empty family is already such a natural transformation and both identities hold componentwise. Since the square was arbitrary, this proves the required lifting property in the functor category.

source.place: Mark Hovey, Model categories, proof of Proposition 5.1.4, printed p. 121: compatible partial lifts give a natural diagonal. Agent expansion includes the empty ordinal.

proof_origin.place: Generalization of Mark Hovey, Model categories, Definition 5.1.1 and Definition 5.1.2 (printed p. 120), and the latching induction in the proof of Proposition 5.1.4 (printed p. 121; PDF pages 130-131 in one-based numbering). Read online, not archived locally. The argument is supplied for ordinal diagrams from pairwise lifting, without model-category assumptions; total recursion is made explicit. The historical blueprint paragraph contains only the finite derived adjunction calculation.
